articles.title: Four years on, Marcos’ door for comms chiefs still revolving
articles.summary: Is sixth time the charm for President Marcos in this rather volatile Cabinet post?

blocks.text: LINO CAYETANO. TV director and producer Lino Cayetano during the 2025 election campaign. He ran for Taguig 1st District congressman.
Lino Cayetano's Facebook page
Is sixth time the charm for President Marcos in this rather volatile Cabinet post?

Just over a year after announcing a new communications secretary, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. found himself in familiar territory: having to explain the appointment of yet another chief of the Presidential Communications Office (PCO).

Is the sixth time the charm? Lino Cayetano, former Taguig City mayor and PTV-4 general manager, will be taking on a post that’s been occupied by five different people in the past four years of Marcos.

Here’s how Marcos framed Dave Gomez’s exit and Cayetano’s entry in an interview with media on Tuesday, October 13: “The reason that we keep turning, we have this high turnover is because the job keeps changing in terms of what we are trying to put forward.”

Marcos added: “In the beginning, we were talking about policy and now we are talking about — then we started talking about what we had to do in terms of implementation. And then we started having to talk — now we are having to talk about getting more towards the more political aspects of the communications job.”

“So, it keeps changing and that’s why we have to keep restructuring it and to be able to satisfy what… especially the demands that you make upon our Presidential Communications group. So yes, that’s what’s behind that.”
Let’s take a small step back and drill down on a line the President uttered: “Now we are having to talk about getting more towards the more political aspects of the communications job.”
Political? If we’re referring to political pedigree and experience, then new Communications Secretary Lino Cayetano would certainly have much to boast of.

Cayetano is the youngest in the current generation of his clan in politics. He also happens to be estranged from his older siblings, Pia and Alan Peter, who are both senators. All three (plus another sibling) are the children of the late former senator Rene Cayetano.

The youngest of the Cayetano clan in politics has held various posts in government — from barangay (village) chief, to district representative, to mayor. He tried to return to Congress in the 2025 polls but lost to a candidate who was backed by his sister-in-law Lani, Senator Alan Peter’s wife.
The older Cayetanos belong to the minority in the Senate that’s identified with Vice President Sara Duterte, Marcos’ erstwhile ally.
Lino Cayetano was also a film and TV director before joining politics full-time.
But what political aspect of the communications job must the new PCO chief pay attention to?

With just under two years left in the administration, two things would probably be foremost in the minds of Malacañang and the new communications chief: the Marcos administration’s legacy and, in relation to that, setting a favorable environment ahead of the 2028 presidential elections.

Cayetano would be the first communications chief under Marcos to have held an elected position in the past. The first communications secretary under Marcos was vlogger Trixie Cruz-Angeles, who was eased out in the first three months of the Marcos administration.
She was followed by Cheloy Garafil, who chaired the Manila Economic and Cultural Office (MECO) before being appointed secretary general of the House of Representatives.

Cesar Chavez, a radio broadcaster and long-time political communications operative, held the post for just over six months. Before Gomez, former ABS-CBN journalist Jay Ruiz was the administration’s primary communications person for four months.

Gomez, who once worked at Philip Morris International Philippines, at least held on to the position for over a year — despite never having faced the Commission on Appointments (CA). That he was bypassed by the CA is part of why he had to be replaced. Talk, for a while, has been that he would have had a hard time hurdling the CA anyway, precisely because of his previous role in a tobacco giant company.

Will Lino Cayetano at least get close to the length of Garafil’s term (almost two years) — which is to say, will he stay on until the end of this administration? If the President’s statements are any indication, that’ll all depend on the “demands that you make upon our Presidential Communications group.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Prosecution: No denial of due process over withdrawal of three charges vs. Sara Duterte
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel on Tuesday said Vice President Sara Duterte was not being denied due process amid its withdrawal of three of the four Articles of Impeachment against her, saying her…

blocks.text: Published October 13, 2026 7:25pm

The House prosecution panel on Tuesday said Vice President Sara Duterte was not being denied due process amid its withdrawal of three of the four Articles of Impeachment against her, saying her defense lawyers were given ample time to question witnesses.

House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro of Batangas and private prosecutors Lorna Kapunan and Amando Ligutan made the position amid the defense's staunch opposition to the prosecution's bid to drop the three articles, a pleading granted by the Senate impeachment court.

The prosecution decided to drop Article I on confidential fund misuse, Article III on bribery, and Article IV on assassination plot, grave threats, and inciting to sedition against the President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr. and his family.

This was after a week of testimonies from the Anti-Money Laundering Council, bank and insurance firm officials, the Bureau of Internal Revenue, as well as financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera, who were called upon by the prosecution to shed light on the alleged unexplained wealth of the vice president and her husband, lawyer Manases "Mans" Carpio.

Article II remains pending before the Senate impeachment court, relating to the couple's alleged unexplained wealth, including their undeclared assets and non-divestment of business interest amid a constitutional prohibition.

"I do not really understand why they are raising the issue on fairness and injustice when in fact the effect of withdrawal is even the evidence presented by the prosecution on withdrawn articles will no longer be considered by the impeachment court. The defense is under no obligation to present their evidence [on these withdrawn charges]. What is the reason for you to present evidence to answer the allegation when in fact it doesn't exist anymore because the same have been withdrawn already by the prosecution," Luistro said in a press conference.

"And let us remember that during the direct examination by the prosecution, they were given super ample time to conduct their cross [examination]. As a matter of fact, ang dami niyang ipinilabas na mga documents through the big screen na nakita rin ng sambayanang Pilipino. If their purpose is for their evidence to be seen by the public, they have a lot of platforms to do that as has been done regularly by the respondent herself," Luistro added.
Kapunan agreed, saying the vice president should stop playing the victim.

"They always play the victim card. Pagod na po tayo sa sinasabi nilang we are the victims. Wait a minute. Hindi siya ang victim, ang taong bayan ang victim dito (We are so tired of them saying they are the victims. Wait a minute. She is not the victim. It is the public who is the victim here). You're talking about public funds, you're talking about a public officer and the impeachment, an accountability mechanism," Kapunan said.

"They keep on saying she is being persecuted. That is not correct. Who is being unfair here? Who is being unjust? The vice president herself. She refuses to come and defend herself in the impeachment court. And yet she does press conferences saying this trial is a farce. And because she is in a press conference, it was not under oath, she cannot be cross examined and asked clarificatory questions. If that is their style, then they come to court with unclean hands," Kapunan added.
Ligutan also said the defense crying injustice is totally misplaced.

"The term that they used is they were not given opportunity to test the evidence of the prosecution. I beg to disagree. That is totally wrong. They were given the opportunity to cross-examine [witnesses] and present videos, photos, statements, news articles," Ligutan said.

"They cannot say they were deprived of presenting countervailing facts. They cross-examined all our witnesses for hours, for days. The defense cannot say they were not given a fair shake," Ligutan added.
Ultimately, Ligutan said any seasoned trial lawyer knows that withdrawal of charges is a fair game in criminal procedure and thus, the defense team should have been prepared for such.

"If you are into litigation, you should prepare for all contingencies. The dropping of some articles [or cases]… that is a usual occurrence in our courts. The defense should have been more flexible," Ligutan said.
"Saan ka makakakita ng defense team na ayaw 'yung pangyayari na 'yung prosecution is withdrawing charges and banking on one solid Article of Impeachment?" Ligutan said.
(Where do you see a defense team opposing the withdrawing of charges against their client and one solid Article of Impeachment?)
Lead defense counsel Sheila Sison on Tuesday said that after 38 days of trial, the prosecution already spent considerable time and government resources presenting evidence and witnesses.
As such, Sison argued, the public has already been exposed to allegations relating to the three dropped articles while the vice president has yet to refute these.
She maintained, however, that the prosecution's move would not affect the defense panel's presentation of its own evidence. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Spain's King Felipe and Queen Letizia visit Ceuta
articles.summary: The royal couple have arrived for their first-ever visit to the exclave to show solidarity with residents.

image.caption: Felipe is the first Spanish monarch to visit the city in nearly twenty yearsImage: Pedro Nunes/REUTERS

blocks.text: King Felipe VI and his wife Queen Letizia arrived in Ceuta on Tuesday afternoon to talk to local leaders and meet with residents still dealing with a major incident at the border with Morocco over the summer.
The trip marks the first royal visit to Ceuta, and Spain's other exclave in the area Melilla, since Felipe's father Juan Carlos I toured the cities in 2007.
Excited crowds gathered to welcome the royals, with some noting that it felt like national authorities were finally paying attention to their plight.
What happened in Ceuta?
In late July, some 80,000 refugees in Morocco rushed the border fence with Spain. More than 140 people were killed in the scuffle.

The incident threw the city of some 84,000 residents into the international spotlight, with calls from right-wing governments within the European Union to suspend the Schengen free movement agreement with Spain.
How the far right hardened Europe's migration stance

However, it soon became clear that most of the refugees were quickly turned back to Morocco, and because of Ceuta's remote location, none moved on to mainland Europe except a group of at-risk children.

At the same time, locals complained that national officials did little to help with at least 10,000 migrants still in the city, and the alleged human traffickers trying to capitalize on the situation.
Meanwhile, the migrants who have been unable to return to Morocco have accused Spanish police of brutality and other abuses.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has accused organized groups stemming from Russia and Israel for spreading misinformation regarding alleged changes in Spain's immigration rules.

The incident also exposed diplomatic tensions between Spain and Morocco. Morocco does not recognize Madrid's claim to Ceuta, which has been under Spanish control for centuries. It remains to be seen how Rabat will react to Felipe's trip.

articles.title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
articles.summary: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s" continuing the country’s investment in international…

image.caption: Rwanda's President Paul Kagame has invested plenty in sports, with F1 a major coupImage: Bright Emoja/AFP

blocks.text: After nearly 40 years of false starts, motor racing's premier sport is returning to Africa, after Formula 1 announced on Tuesday that Rwanda would soon host a Grand Prix.

The race will be know as the African Grand Prix after a 10-year contract was signed between the parties. With no suitable track ready, Rwanda will build one in Bugesera, southeast of the capital Kigali. F1 said it will be ready "early in the next decade."

The last time F1 raced in Africa was the South African Grand Prix in 1993. While there has since been plenty of talk of the sport returning to the continent, most often South Africa itself, nothing concrete had happened, until now.
A race in every continent

"Today is a landmark moment for Formula 1," F1 President and chief executive Stefano Domenicali said. "With Rwanda joining the calendar from the next decade our sport will race in every inhabited continent, bringing the world championship closer than ever to fans around the globe.

"Africa has always been part of Formula 1's future, and from the beginning we were determined to return in the right way, with the right partner, a long-term commitment and a clear vision for creating meaningful impact."

One of the most vocal proponents of a race in Africa has been seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton. The 41-year-old Black British driver, currently with Ferrari, has said he has been "fighting in the background" for years to have a race in Africa. With the date not yet set in stone for the African Grand Prix, it remains to be seen whether he can prolong his career enough to be on the grid when the lights go out in Rwanda.
Kagame all in on sports but sportswashing claims loom

For Rwandan President Paul Kagame, the event is "a success and a milestone for the entire continent, especially for the African fans." He added that he hoped it could lead to more F1 events in Africa.

Kagame has been president of Rwanda for 25 years and essentially ran the country for the six years before that after the genocide in 1994. He routinely wins over 99% of the vote in elections in a country often criticized for its human rights record.

blocks.caption: Bayern Munich ended a commercial deal with 'Visit Rwanda' last yearImage: Bernd Feil/M.i.S./IMAGO

blocks.text: The 68-year-old has bet big on sports. Rwanda has had sponsorship deals with a number of top European football clubs, including Arsenal, Atletico Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich. However, fan and media backlash over the deal caused Bayern to drop the commercial element with the country's tourist arm, Visit Rwanda, last year. Arsenal did not renew its deal. Many critics have labeled the policy as sportswashing.
The country also has deals with top US basketball and American Football teams, and hosted cycling's Road World Championships last year.
But Formula 1, one of the world's richest sports, will likely be seen as Kagame and Rwanda's biggest sporting coup to date.

articles.title: EXPLAINER: What 'piercing the corporate veil' means
articles.summary: The doctrine of piercing the corporate veil has been raised during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, as defense and prosecution lawyers debated the assets and earnings of…

blocks.text: Published October 13, 2026 7:16pm

The doctrine of piercing the corporate veil has been raised during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, as defense and prosecution lawyers debated the assets and earnings of companies linked to Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio.

The issue arose after Atty. Alexander Cabrera, a financial forensic analyst presented as a prosecution witness, testified that Duterte and Carpio supposedly had unexplained wealth and undeclared assets amounting to P817.87 million.

Cabrera said he arrived at the figure by piercing the corporate veil, a legal doctrine that allows courts, under certain circumstances, to disregard a corporation’s separate legal personality and hold the individuals behind it accountable.
Defense lead counsel Sheila Sison later challenged Cabrera’s testimony, describing his conclusions as “unbridled and erroneous conclusions of law and fact.”

She cited the Supreme Court’s ruling in Kukan International Corporation v. Reyes, which states that "wrongdoing must be established clearly and convincingly before a corporation’s separate juridical personality can be disregarded," and that such wrongdoing "cannot be presumed."
“Otherwise an injustice that was never intended may result from an erroneous application. And it bears reiterating that piercing the veil of corporate fiction is frowned upon,” Sison said.
When can the corporate veil be pierced?

In its ruling, the Supreme Court said the doctrine may be applied when a corporation’s separate legal personality is used to “defeat public convenience, justify wrong, protect fraud, or defend crime, or when it serves as a shield to confuse legitimate issues."

The doctrine may also apply when a corporation is "merely the alter ego or business conduit of an individual, or when its organization, control and operations effectively make it an instrumentality, agency or extension of another person or corporation."

The High Court also explained that while a corporation may be established for any lawful purpose, courts may treat it as "an association of persons or merge two corporations into one when their separate legal identities are used to conceal fraud or illegality."
In such cases, the corporate structure cannot be used to shield those responsible from liability.
Sison said she cited the ruling to "avoid misleading the public" watching the impeachment proceedings.

She questioned the basis of Cabrera’s conclusions, saying the witness had repeatedly acknowledged that he had insufficient time to conduct his analysis and did not have all the documents needed to form a sufficient basis for a complete opinion.

“Now that witness has answered over time and repeatedly that unang una sa lahat, wala siyang sapat na oras. Pangalawa, hindi niya hawak ang lahat ng dokumento to form sufficient basis or ng kumpletong opinyon,” Sison said.

(That witness has repeatedly answered that, first and foremost, he did not have sufficient time. Second, he did not have all the documents needed to establish a sufficient basis for a complete opinion.)
Diokno moved to strike Sison’s characterization of Cabrera’s testimony as “erroneous,” arguing that it was a legal conclusion and was “totally out of order.”

“It’s up to the Honorable Court to decide whether the opinion of Atty. Cabrera is acceptable or not. And it’s not in our place, whether I’m for the prosecution or for the defense, to make such irresponsible statements. I move to strike, Your Honor,” Diokno said.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero, however, ruled that Sison’s remarks would remain on the record.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Climate change poses a challenge to earthquake, tsunami preparedness -- OCD
articles.summary: Climate change has made it more challenging for agencies and stakeholders to prepare for earthquakes and tsunamis as it leaves them with less time to respond to potential disasters, the Office of…

blocks.text: Published October 13, 2026 7:02pm

Climate change has made it more challenging for agencies and stakeholders to prepare for earthquakes and tsunamis as it leaves them with less time to respond to potential disasters, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said Tuesday.

During the World Tsunami Awarness Day press conference in Quezon City, OCD-NCR director George Keyser said the return period of major natural events has become shorter and more intense over time due to climate change.
These natural events include storms and earthquakes.
"Malaki talaga ang epekto ng climate change (sa disaster preparedness)," Keyser said. "Paikli ng paikli yung return period."
(Climate change has greatly affected disaster preparedness. the return period of natural events has become shorter.)
This led agencies like OCD to conduct several meetings with stakeholders in order revise intial preparedness and response plans.
Aside from climate change, Keyser said the lax perception of the public about disasters is also a challenge when it come to preparedness.
"Yung number one challenge talaga ito, yung perception na baka hindi man mangyari yan. Yung mabala na, yung ayaw mag-prepare," the OCD official said.
(The number one challenge is the perception of the public about disasters that it may not happen. Those who do not want to prepare.)
He added that Metro Manila must also have a locally appropriated evacuation plan to address situations when road and communication disruption take place after an earthquake.
"Kaya tayo nag-di-drill para makita yung lapses na itong sector. So yan, inaaral yan," Keyser said.
(We conduct drills to see the lapses of each sector and study it.)

Meanwhile, geologist Charmaine Villamil of the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) explained changes in the climate do not trigger the occurrence of an earthquake but can aggravate its effects.
"Changes in the climate will not trigger the occurrence of earthquake, but the effects of climate change can aggravate the effects of tsunami," Villamil said.
"Kapag dumating yung tsunami, mas mataas pa po yung aasahan na alon," she added.
(Once a tsunami occurs, expect higher waves.)
The United Nation has designated every November 5 as World Tsunami Awareness Day to promote preparedness for natural disasters.
This include urging the public to participate in drills, runs, or walks along tsunami evacuation routes to help build resilience.
For its part, the PHIVOLCS will hold the “Tsunami! Run for Safety: Shake, Drop, or Roar? Move Away from the Shore!” on October 24 in Pasay City. — LA, GMA News

articles.title: Is punishing the poor Trump’s last hand to play?
articles.summary:
The pre-midterm defenestration of ACA enrollees looks like political madness – but the president appears to believe hitting poor people might work for him

There is a manic quality to

blocks.text: There is a manic quality to Donald Trump’s desperate dash to do something, anything, ahead of November’s midterm elections to convince beleaguered Americans that he can make the pressures his policies have imposed on their livelihoods go away.

The US president offered to lower barriers against beef imports to limit surging meat prices, only to consider backtracking under pressure from the cow lobby. He offered to stop diesel exports, only to find oil companies were not interested. He weakened fuel efficiency standards, claiming this would trim the price of a new car (and forgetting to point out it will also raise spending on gas.) In early October he started mailing $500 checks to nearly a million people touting his healthcare “wins”. Oh, and he promised adult Americans a $5,000 check if Republicans maintain control of Congress. That, too, will go nowhere.

In the face of such setbacks, maybe Trump felt he had to demonstrate he still can get something done. Still, it is somewhat counterintuitive that the administration, in the shape of Vice-President JD Vance, decided to broadcast the one initiative it did manage to bring to fruition: ejecting more than 750,000 enrollees from the Affordable Care Act (ACA) health insurance marketplaces, on grounds that they are not entitled to federal subsidies.

Trump could argue that the cuts fit within the administration’s promised commitment to restore fiscal discipline. But that part of the platform – which came as Scott Bessent, the treasury secretary, promised to trim the budget deficit to 3% of US gross domestic product – was never more than a rhetorical feint.

The pre-midterm defenestration of ACA enrollees by Trump’s “fraud taskforce”, by contrast, looks a lot like political madness, given the persistent economic anxieties articulated by Democratic and Republican voters across the country.

The savings from the ACA maneuver, estimated by the administration at $2.2bn per year, are chump change compared to the centerpiece of Trump’s fiscal policy – the One Big Beautiful Bill Act from 2025 that is expected to add $4.1tn to budget deficits over the next decade, largely due to tax cuts benefiting the most affluent Americans.

Pace Bessent, the budget deficit is growing rapidly, expected to rise to some $2tn in the fiscal year of 2026, roughly 6% of GDP and some 18% more than in fiscal 2024, the last year of the Biden administration.

Rather than stem budgetary red ink, it’s as if Trump’s objective is to spread misery beyond the 3 million Americans who had to drop their health insurance after the administration last year cancelled subsidies offered by the Biden administration.

blocks.caption: Kimberly Brandt of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services holds up a poster depicting a headshot of Cory Lloyd, convicted of Affordable Care Act fraud, as Mehmet Oz speaks during a conference on 22 September in Washington DC.  Photograph: Andrew Harnik/Getty Images

blocks.text: The effort is something out of the playbook of Elon Musk’s Doge. His promise to rid the government of “waste” and “fraud” probably caused the deaths of millions of children in the developing world after the dismantling of USAID, but proved largely irrelevant to the task of saving money for the government. It may serve as a masterclass in trolling. But it is not a vote-winner.

Part of Trump’s brain seems to understand this. Trump paid in part for the “beautiful” bill’s colossal tax cut by cutting funding to Medicaid and the Snap food stamp program for low-income Americans. But he engineered most of the cuts to kick in after the midterms to minimize the political cost. The thinking was that lower-income Americans would happily vote for the Republicans out of gratitude for their somewhat bigger tax refund checks this year and tax breaks for overtime and tips (cleverly designed to expire at the end of Trump’s term) and not notice the cuts rushing down the pike on federal programs they relied on.
after newsletter promotion

But the new evictions from the ACA suggest that his brain’s darker side is winning. Indeed, it underscores Trump’s belief that hitting poor people might work for him. Rather than a commitment to sound fiscal policy, a helping hand for American families treading water or an economic platform of any kind, Trump’s latest exercise in “fraud prevention” points to a strategy revolving around punishing people he can define as “bad”. Deep underwater in the polls for his nutty stewardship of the economy, among other things, Trump seems to believe that his one remaining winning card is to do violence against constituencies that his base may not like. Top of the list are immigrants and low-income people. And so it is that ICE is also doubling down, announcing it will hire another 5,000 agents by the end of the year.

The president is on to something. About two-thirds of Republicans believe giving more aid to the poor does more harm than good, according to surveys from the Pew Research Center. Despite the repeated instances of abuse by federal agents, only 19% of Republicans think the Trump administration is doing too much to deport immigrants illegally in the country. The most radical rightwing voters are all in for federal deportations and don’t think the federal government should be responsible for ensuring Americans’ healthcare.

Perhaps Trump’s heart truly lies on the dark side. But doubling down on policies to please the most ardent fanatics in his base ultimately reveals the weakness of Trump’s position. Perhaps even he understands that he has lost the rest of the country. Punishing the poor and the foreign – alongside an unlikely $5,000 Hail Mary pass – is all he has left.

items: Eduardo Porter is a journalist focused on economics and politics. He writes the newsletter Being There on Substack

articles.title: UK asks Interpol to reject Argentina’s ‘politically motivated’ requests for Falklands oil arrests
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Caution urged over Javier Milei government’s ‘red notice’ requests for arrest of individuals linked to oil project

Britain has appealed to Interpol to reject Argentina’s requests…
articles.byline: Daniel Boffey in Port Stanley, Falkland islands

blocks.text: Britain has appealed to Interpol to reject Argentina’s requests for the arrest of individuals involved in a large oil project off the Falkland Islands.

With tensions over the sovereignty of the British overseas territory reaching levels not seen since the war with Argentina in 1982, UK officials have sought urgent assurances from the international organisation.

A letter has been sent to Interpol’s headquarters in Lyon arguing that “red notice” requests from Argentina for the arrest of such individuals, including British nationals, should be seen as politically motivated.
It is understood that the UK government is concerned by what sources suggested was an attempt to bully people and companies out of working in the Falklands.

An oil project known as Sea Lion in the north Falklands basin in the south Atlantic has the potential to triple the Falklands’ GDP but Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has vowed to block it. Argentina’s strategy includes attempts to criminalise those involved in Sea Lion and deter other investors.
In its letter, the UK government has urged Interpol to be cautious in its handling of Argentinian requests for detentions, it is understood.

Andrea Clausen, the chief executive of the Falklands government, confirmed that the use of Interpol by Argentina was a threat but added: “One would hope that Interpol wouldn’t necessarily take action.”
She said: “Certainly those of us who have an interest have had a look at certain sections of Interpol’s constitution to see what we think it could mean.”

It is understood that a response from Interpol to the UK government’s correspondence stated that it would respect article 3 of its constitution, which forbids it from undertaking any intervention or activities of a political character.

Interpol screens red notices, which are requests to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition. If circulated to the enforcement agencies, individual member countries then decide whether to act on the requests. Nearly 20,000 were issued last year.
The Foreign Office has been approached for comment.

The intensity of the Argentinian menace relating to the Falklands is at a level that UK officials say has not been seen since the war 44 years ago that followed the invasion ordered by Argentina’s dictator Gen Leopoldo Galtieri.
The 74-day conflict ended with the surrender of the Argentinian forces and cost the lives of 649 of its military personnel, 255 British military personnel and three Falkland islanders.

Argentina continues to claim sovereignty over the 700 islands that make up the Falklands and has dismissed a 2013 referendum in which 99.8% of the islands’ 3,600 residents voted to remain a British territory, with only three votes against.

Despite Interpol’s reassurance about its screening of red notice requests, concerns remain that Argentina could convince the organisation’s member states that its requests are not political but rooted in domestic legislation.
Milei has initiated criminal proceedings against the Israeli company Navitas and its British partner, Rockhopper Exploration, which are the core companies in the offshore Sea Lion project.
after newsletter promotion
A draft national sovereignty introduced to Argentina’s congress would further expand the scope of sanctions to affiliates of those companies, financial intermediaries, shareholders and suppliers.

The bill additionally contains clauses that could target those involved in the fishing industry in the Falklands, which makes up a large part of the islands’ economy. The archipelago is 300 miles (500km) east of the southern Patagonian coast of Argentina.

Workers in the oil and fisheries sectors on the Falklands – known in Argentina as Las Malvinas – are understood to be concerned that they could be targeted should they travel, particularly to South America where there is support for Buenos Aires’s sovereignty claim.

In a tandem move to kill off Sea Lion, Argentina is expected within 24 hours to escalate further its dispute with the UK by requesting arbitration under annexe VII of the UN convention on the law of the sea (Unclos) over the oil project.

On 28 September, Milei gave the UK a two-week deadline to stop the project or face such a legal action. The deadline passed on Monday and Argentinian newspapers said an application for arbitration would follow.

Under it, Buenos Aires will claim that the UK is in breach of a UN resolution inviting the parties to negotiate over the sovereignty dispute and refrain from “unilateral modifications” to the situation. It will be seeking a binding ruling that the UK must stop the drilling. However, UK government sources are confident that Unclos will not wade into a sovereignty dispute.

At a public meeting on Monday evening, one of the Falkland Islands’ assembly members, Dean Dent, told constituents that the UK government was working hard on a tough response to the Argentinian Unclos threat.

“The UK government has assembled quite an in-depth team of legal advisers, KCs – that is the first step,” he said. “There have been four recent similar cases where a case of sovereignty has been taken to Unclos and all four were disregarded by the tribunal as all four cases were a sovereignty issue, not a maritime issue.”

The UK government is expected to be increasingly muscular in its approach to Argentina in the coming days. The prime minister, Andy Burnham, told parliament on Monday that he had raised the issue and “the clear and declared will of the islanders to remain British” with the US president, Donald Trump.

articles.title: Ian McKellen to star in UK premiere of ‘mixed reality’ play – but not in person
articles.summary:
Audiences in Manchester will be asked to wear smart glasses for An Ark, which debuted in New York this year

Ian McKellen will star in a groundbreaking new play that gets its UK premiere in…

blocks.text: Ian McKellen will star in a groundbreaking new play that gets its UK premiere in Manchester next spring. But the veteran actor will not set foot on stage.

The Lord of the Rings star is taking part in An Ark, a “mixed reality” play that had its debut in New York earlier this year. Theatregoers are asked to wear smart glasses, which project the actors into the room.

John McGrath, the chief executive of Factory International, which is putting on the play, said: “Mixed reality is when you see both the virtual elements of an experience and also the real world around you.”

He said it differed from virtual reality because rather than putting on “a set of goggles that exclude the physical reality you’re in”, these glasses “project into the space but also show the real world you are in”.

Asked whether McKellen would have any physical role in the play, which will be on at Aviva Studios from 27 March to 10 April, he said: “His virtual presence will be there. He may well come and visit the play but you won’t see the real Ian McKellen performing.”

blocks.caption: Four actors were filmed by 52 cameras in one take for the play. Photograph: Tin Drum

blocks.text: He said the audience would be satisfied to pay to attend a play where the actors were not there in the flesh. “When people go to see a film, you don’t spend time explaining the lead actors in the film won’t be in the cinema. This is no different,” he said.

The 47-minute production is billed as an exploration of life and death, during which “actors share stories about life to make it seem as if they are right before you, offering an intimate reimagining of live theatre. With that technology, actors share stories about how humans grow, connect, and grieve over a life.”

While some may think going to the theatre is exciting because you see the actors performing live in front of you, McGrath said mixed reality plays had other benefits. “What you get is the intimacy with the actors, so you feel like they are sitting in front of you and talking directly to you.” He said this created a “very touching personal experience”.
Four actors, including McKellen, were filmed by 52 cameras in one take at a studio in the French city of Grenoble. They appear seated just before the viewer as if they are putting on a private show.

blocks.caption: Ian McKellen takes his turn during filming for the mixed reality play. Photograph: Tin Drum

blocks.text: For the actors, McGrath said, “it is far closer to being in a film than being on stage. It’s one for actors who enjoy a new challenge.”
The theatre plans to hold public events to explore the future and ethics of this technology.
Factory’s programme for 2027 celebrates 20 years of the organisation. Among the plans is a special production of Philip Glass’s opera Einstein on the Beach.

McGrath said: “This be one of the biggest opera performances anywhere in the year – it’s Philip Glass’s 90th birthday year, and this is the first time in 50 years there has been a full new production of it. It will be a way to experience that amazing score in a big, huge warehouse in a way that’s very different to an opera you’d usually see.”
He added: “Most of the work in this programme, we are either the world premiere or the UK premiere and we have co-produced it.”

blocks.text: Good morning. Ilhan Omar has said she will not be silenced after federal agents raided her home. In a social media post, the Minnesota congresswoman criticized the raid as an attempt by the Trump administration “to target political enemies and weaponize law enforcement”.

Donald Trump and key allies have accused Omar of fraud related to her family’s immigration history, fantasizing openly about denaturalizing her and expelling her from the country. Omar said in her post: “This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”

House Democratic leaders, including minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, party whip Katherine Clark and caucus chair Pete Aguilar, issued a joint statement excoriating the president for the search, calling it “deeply disturbing”. blocks.text: A federal judge has ordered Donald Trump’s administration to temporarily halt the broadcast of taxpayer-funded television ads promoting the president ahead of the 3 November midterm elections. The administration “shall not enter into, renew, or expand any agreement authorizing the development, creation, dissemination, placement, or airing of the … advertisements,” the judge said in her ruling. She also ordered the administration to cancel the remaining portion of a $20m advertising purchase, halting further spending on the campaign.
Anti-vaxxers target Texas measles doctors to cast doubt on deaths amid outbreak

blocks.caption: An MMR vaccine being prepared. Photograph: Mary Conlon/AP

blocks.text: Amid rising measles outbreaks and fatalities across the US, anti-vaccine activists – including figures such as HHS Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr and Children’s Health Defense – are actively working to dispute official death tolls and cast doubt on the virus’s severity.

To deflect accountability for the resurgence of preventable disease, these groups are promoting claims that patient deaths stem from medical error and inappropriate treatment rather than measles complications, even filing formal medical board complaints against treating pediatricians.
Public health experts and physicians warn that this playbook fuels distrust, vilifies frontline healthcare workers, and distracts from the core issue of declining vaccination rates

blocks.caption: Cocaine hidden in ship off the Canary Islands. Photograph: Policía Nacional

blocks.text: A four-month investigation by the Guardian has revealed that the surge in cocaine trafficking to Europe is directly linked to the expanding presence of Latin American criminal networks in Europe, where they have forged close ties with local mafia organisations.

The investigation, utilising databases, police and intelligence agencies, along with interviews with judges, prosecutors and experts from eight countries, shows that cartels and factions from Colombia, Brazil, Ecuador, Venezuela, Mexico and the US are active in at least 12 European countries. The figure could be even higher, as it includes only groups officially identified in Europe and does not include gangs that lack a physical presence in Europe while working in “joint ventures” with European mafias.

articles.title: Hurricane Simon, storm Rachel leave 5 dead in western Mexico
articles.summary: Hurricane Simon pounded western Mexico, causing one death in the state of Guerrero, while four people died and some are missing in the state of Baja California due to the impact of post-tropical…

image.caption: Waves from post-tropical cyclone Rachel crash into beachfront homes in Long Beach, Calif., on Monday. At least four people died in the state of Baja California, Mexico, due to Rachel's impact. (Jae C. Hong/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

Hurricane Simon pounded western Mexico, causing one death in the state of Guerrero, while four people died and some are missing in the state of Baja California due to the impact of post-tropical cyclone Rachel.
Hurricane Simon approaches Mexico's Pacific Coast, with potential landfall later in week
Hurricane Simon pounded western Mexico with more wind and rain on Monday after tropical weather systems caused five deaths and damage in Pacific coastal towns and resorts.
The eye of the Category 2 hurricane remained offshore as its outer bands of winds and rain slammed communities between the Sierra Madre and the Pacific Ocean, near Puerto Vallarta.
Flood advisories were mostly lifted in the southwestern U.S. after the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel caused weekend flooding in Las Vegas.

In Mexico's Baja California state, rescuers on Monday combed parts of the coastal city of Ensenada where floodwaters swept away vehicles and damaged homes. At least four people died in the state due to the impact of post-tropical cyclone Rachel.
Resident Johana Nuriulu said the flooding began during the night, shortly after heavy rain knocked out electricity.
"We heard a loud noise that sounded like ocean waves, but really loud," she said.
A person rides a bicycle through a flooded street in San Francisco, also known as San Pancho, off Mexico's Pacific Coast. (Christian Ruano/Reuters)

Nuriulu said she went outside and discovered that a nearby stream had overflowed, sending water rushing through the neighbourhood. The waters inundated streets and homes, sweeping away vehicles and other belongings.
"Everything was being dragged away," Nuriulu said.
Several communities were cut off by landslides and overflowing rivers elsewhere in Baja California.
In the afternoon, the Mexican military used helicopters to rescue 32 people — 22 of them foreigners — from a ranch in Ensenada. Baja California Gov. Marina del Pilar Avila said 13 were youths.
The state secretary of security, Gen. Laureano Carrillo, said that some of the group were missionaries meeting at the ranch and that among them were Germans and Americans.
6 missing in Baja California

Baja California civil protection co-ordinator Ignacio Lozoya said Monday evening that four bodies had been recovered in Ensenada: a 13-year-old girl on Sunday, and two women and a 4-year-old boy on Monday. Lozoya said six people remained missing: four in Ensenada and two from the town of San Felipe, a father and son who went fishing Saturday and did not return.
According to Avila, some 14,000 federal and state personnel had been deployed across Baja California to assist affected residents and respond to the emergency.
A drone view shows waves crash against beachfront buildings as Hurricane Simon remains off Mexico's Pacific coast, in San Pancho. (Christian Ruano/Reuters)

To the south, Simon downed trees and electricity poles, blocked roads and flooded homes in coastal towns of Guerrero state, including the major seaport of Acapulco, Gov. Evelyn Salgado said at a news conference.
A 71-year-old man died after a wall collapsed in Chilpancingo, Guerrero's capital, Salgado said.

Simon had maximum sustained winds of 155 km/h late Monday and was expected to remain a hurricane through midweek, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said Monday evening. It was slowly approaching the western Mexico coast, where heavy rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides before landfall possibly late Friday.

In Puerto Vallarta, workers removed wooden panels from boarded-up storefronts and businesses reopened Monday as rains eased. The popular tourist destination's international airport suspended operations until Tuesday morning.

Rachel weakened into a post-tropical cyclone as it moved north into Southern California. The storm battered the coast with unusually large waves, which tore apart a boardwalk and smashed into homes in Long Beach. Some residents were forced to evacuate.

articles.title: New HVAC training center opens as El Niño raises the stakes for cooling efficiency
articles.summary: The Philippines’ growing need for reliable cooling extends beyond homes and offices. As the country braces for a strong to very strong El Niño expected to persist into the first half of 2027,…

blocks.text: The Philippines’ growing need for reliable cooling extends beyond homes and offices. As the country braces for a strong to very strong El Niño expected to persist into the first half of 2027, according to PAGASA, efficient air conditioning is also an important consideration for businesses and industries that depend on controlled temperatures and uninterrupted operations.

LG Electronics Philippines is expanding its focus on this market with the opening of its HVAC Academy and Business Innovation Center in Silver City, Pasig, on October 9. The facility combines technical training for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) professionals with demonstrations of LG’s commercial technologies, including systems designed for larger buildings and industrial applications.

The opening comes as LG looks to expand its commercial cooling business in the Philippines, where demand for data centers and other digital infrastructure is creating opportunities for more specialized HVAC systems.
Cooling becomes an industrial requirement

The importance of cooling is particularly evident in data centers, where temperature control is necessary to keep servers and other computing equipment operating reliably. As businesses expand their use of cloud services and artificial intelligence, facilities must manage the heat generated by increasingly demanding computing workloads.

LG Electronics Philippines sales manager Vanlee Budod told the media present that data centers have become a priority for the company’s global business. “Our main target, actually, LG Global’s main target right now are data centers,” Budod said.

The company expects demand for commercial and industrial cooling solutions to increase over the next one to two years as the Philippines develops its digital infrastructure. Beyond data centers, LG identifies semiconductor facilities, healthcare environments, commercial real estate, hospitality, and smart buildings as markets that require reliable and efficient HVAC systems.

El Niño adds another consideration for Philippine businesses. PAGASA’s October 7 advisory warned that the ongoing phenomenon could intensify into a very strong event and continue through the first half of 2027, increasing the likelihood of below-normal rainfall and dry spells or drought in some areas. While the effects will vary by location, businesses must contend with the operational demands of cooling in a country already exposed to high temperatures.

Energy efficiency is therefore relevant alongside cooling capacity. HVAC systems can account for a substantial share of a building’s energy use, depending on its design and operations. Equipment selection, proper installation, maintenance, and controls all affect how efficiently a system performs.
Training engineers for more complex systems

LG’s new HVAC Academy is designed to develop the technical skills needed to specify, install, commission, troubleshoot, and maintain these systems. Its training covers engineering design and simulation, advanced HVAC equipment, smart building controls, and cloud-based management.

The facility includes learning opportunities involving variable refrigerant flow (VRF) systems, heat pumps, chillers, and centralized controls. These technologies serve different applications, from individual commercial buildings to larger facilities with more demanding cooling requirements.

The emphasis on technical training reflects the work involved in keeping HVAC systems operating as intended. Selecting suitable equipment is only one part of the process. Poor installation, incorrect commissioning, or inadequate maintenance can undermine system performance, including its energy efficiency and reliability.

The academy is intended for mechanical contractors, consulting and specifying engineers, commissioning technicians, facilities managers, maintenance engineers, and LG’s own technical and business teams. The company also plans to use the facility to help customers understand how its equipment can be applied to their projects.

According to LG, the Pasig academy follows the opening of a similar facility in Cebu in 2025. Budod said that the company aims to hold at least four training sessions a week, accommodating around 10 to 20 participants per session. Training is offered free of charge, with some participants eligible for internal LG certification after completing the required assessment.
LG is also considering a partnership with the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority, although no formal agreement or timetable has been announced.
Beyond air conditioning

The Business Innovation Center, which shares the Pasig facility with the academy, showcases other parts of LG’s business-to-business portfolio. These include information displays for commercial, educational, and hospitality settings, IT solutions, and commercial laundry equipment.

The broader facility gives customers and industry professionals a place to examine LG technologies and discuss potential applications with the company’s teams. For its HVAC business, the academy also provides a venue for developing the technical knowledge required as cooling systems become more specialized.

LG is preparing for possible growth in the Philippine data center market as demand for AI and cloud services expands. Budod said the company was monitoring developments in the country’s participation in the US-led Pax Silica initiative, while emphasizing that LG was preparing for potential business opportunities rather than announcing a confirmed project.
“That’s their comment, but for us, we’re just preparing,” Budod affirmed

The company’s investment in training comes as cooling requirements extend across more sectors of the economy. For data centers, cooling supports the operation of computing infrastructure. For commercial buildings and industrial facilities, it affects equipment reliability, working conditions, and energy consumption. Developing the workforce capable of designing and maintaining these systems will be part of meeting that demand.

blocks.text: Published October 13, 2026 6:19pm
A graduate of Central Mindanao University took the top spot in the licensure examination for professional foresters, given earlier this month.

According to the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), 1,406 test takers out of 1,892 passed the exam, given by the Board for Foresters at test enters in Metro Manila, Baguio, Butuan, Cagayan de Oro, Cebu, Davao, Iloilo, Koronadal, Legazpi, Lucena, Pagadian, Pampanga, Rosales, Tacloban and Tuguegarao.

Joey Siarez Jumawan of Central Mindanao University achieved the highest score of 94.10%, while the top performing school with 50 or more examinees is the University of the Philippines-Los Baños, with all 129 of its test takers passing.

articles.title: Bulgaria condemns Black Sea drone attacks as Russia's war in Ukraine spills over into Eastern Europe
articles.summary: Bulgaria has seen the second spate of drone attacks on merchant ships off its coast in the past week. Russia has been accused of repeatedly targeting civilian cargo ships in the area.

image.caption: Bulgarian police said they were able to rescue all affected crew membersImage: Bulphoto Agency/REUTERS

blocks.text: Two ships were struck by drones off the coast of Bulgaria on Tuesday, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said, the second such incident in the Black Sea in the past week.
He wrote in a social media post that one ship, a Ukrainian-owned cargo vessel, was "hit by three aerial drones," shortly before another ship was struck.

"We lack solid, clear evidence to level accusations against any specific party; however... logic suggests the outcome works to the advantage of the Russian Federation," Radev added, also confirming that no one had been killed.
The origin of last week's attack is also unknown, but Moscow is also suspected in that incident.
Radev said that the escalation of violence in the Black Sea was "unacceptable" and that he would be summoning the Russian ambassador to discuss it.
Conflict spills over into Eastern Europe
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also condemned the attacks, calling them "another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine".
"We stand with Bulgaria and thank its rescuers for their swift response. Those responsible should be held accountable," she said in a statement.
At least 45 merchant vessels have been struck by drones in the Black Sea in the past 12 months, as Russia's war has increasingly taken a toll on Eastern Europe.
Radev said he had requested official assistance from the EU and NATO to determine the exact source of the recent attacks.

articles.title: Hobbs and Whistles owner investigates hack that may have exposed customer data
articles.summary: Cyber-attack on TFG London comes less than a week after online fashion seller Asos was hit by hackers

blocks.text: The owner of Phase Eight, Hobbs and Whistles has warned that its websites and IT systems have been hit by a cyber-attack that may have compromised customers’ personal data.

The South-African listed TFG London said that it had identified the “cybersecurity incident” at the three UK-based retail chains on Sunday. Its two other UK brands – Inside Story and White Stuff – are not affected.
TFG said its stores have stayed open and trading but some of its IT systems “remain unavailable” and it has paused all online orders as a “precautionary measure”.
An “investigation is ongoing, including establishing whether any personal or other sensitive information has been compromised,” the company said.
If the investigation establishes any personal information has been accessed by hackers TFG said it would “notify affected individuals or organisations.”

“Some of our brand’s website capabilities may not be available as the investigation continues. We apologise for any disruption and will provide additional updates to our customers as appropriate,” the company added.
TFG’s operations in Africa or Australia run on separate systems and are not affected.
It has engaged external cybersecurity specialists to contain the incident, which has been reported to the relevant UK authorities.

The attack on the three UK fashion brands comes less than a week after a cyber-attack affected online fashion seller Asos in which the names, addresses and recent search data of millions of customers was accessed.

H&M said on Monday that it was also investigating claims that its systems had been attacked. However, the fast fashion retailer said: “We have not found any indications that our data environment has been compromised.”
after newsletter promotion

Several other British retailers, including Marks & Spencer, the Co-op and Harrods, suffered damaging cyber incidents last year. M&S and the Co-op experienced stock shortages, and the former was forced to shut down its website for several weeks while it ensured its systems were clean.

Marijus Briedis, the chief technology officer at the digital security firm NordVPN, said: “Coming so soon after the Asos incident, this latest attack on TFG London is another reminder that the retail sector is firmly in hackers’ sights. These attacks are becoming a recurring nightmare for businesses, and there’s every reason to believe we’ll see more of them.

“Retailers are particularly attractive targets because they hold valuable customer information and rely on a sprawling network of payment systems, suppliers and third-party technology providers. Every connection is a potential weak point, and attackers are increasingly adept at exploiting stolen credentials, human error and gaps in security.”

articles.title: Trump targets Ilhan Omar at rally following raid on her home – US politics live
articles.summary: President says Somalia, birthplace of the Minnesota Democratic congresswoman, is ‘one of the worst countries on the planet’

blocks.text: Key events

items: 21m agoCongresswoman Omar says she will 'not be silenced' as Trump targets her at rally following raid

blocks.text: Donald Trump on Monday tried to boost senator Jon Husted’s reelection campaign by attacking two groups of immigrants during a rally in Ohio.

Trump also gave a shoutout to representative Max Miller, the Republican congressman who refused to stop running for reelection after facing accusations of domestic abuse, pointing him out in the audience.
“Thank you, Max, for coming,” Trump said. “Thank you. Very good.”

Trump focused, however, on a favorite issue — immigration. Trump has long targeted Minnesota’s large population of Somali immigrants and on Monday he linked that group to Haitians in Springfield, Ohio.

During a presidential debate two years ago, Trump falsely accused the latter group of eating pets. Referencing those allegations Monday, Trump said “I was right” and boasted that Haitians were being driven out of the country by his administration’s policies .

“If you want to stop Ohio from being plundered, ransacked and destroyed like Minnesota is being destroyed, we’re going to stop it,” Trump said. “Just like we did with Springfield, we’re going to stop it, we’re not going to let it happen.”
Congresswoman Omar says she will 'not be silenced' as Trump targets her at rally following raid
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Minnesota congresswoman Ilhan Omar said she will “not be silenced” and called a search of her Washington home part of President Donald Trump’s “intimidation” campaign.
Democratic representative Omar, an outspoken critic of the president, said she was being targeted as one of the Republican’s “political enemies”.
It comes as Trump targeted the congresswoman during a rally in Youngstown, Ohio, last night. He said Somalia, where Omar was born, is “one of the worst countries ⁠anywhere on the planet”.
He said:
double quotation markShe comes from one of the worst countries ⁠anywhere on the planet. What a mess they have done - Somalia.

He urged supporters to vote Republican “if you want to stop Ohio from being plundered, ransacked and destroyed like Minnesota’s being destroyed”. In response, the crowd of Republican supporters chanted: “Deport, deport.”
US authorities conducted a predawn raid of Omar’s home in Washington, DC, on Monday as part of an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said.

A person familiar with the investigation said it is ⁠related to alleged immigration fraud, and part of ⁠the probe concerns the Somali-born lawmaker’s immigration paperwork filled out ​by her late father when she was a child.
Omar wrote on social media that the US government is being weaponized to target a political enemy of the president.
“For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns,” she said. “This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”

In a statement, US House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries and other members of the party’s leadership in the chamber said the raid was “deeply disturbing and raises serious questions” about the weaponization of the federal government against Trump’s enemies.
In other developments:

items: A federal judge has ordered Donald Trump’s administration to temporarily halt the broadcast of taxpayer-funded television ads promoting the president ahead of the 3 November midterm elections. Effective as of 6.45pm ET on Sunday, US district judge Jennifer L Rochon of the southern district of New York issued a temporary restraining order aimed at the ads that is meant to stay in effect for at least 14 days.

The New York mayor, Zohran Mamdani, compared US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)’s recent shooting of a man in the Manhattan enclave of Marble Hill to a mass shooting scene – and called for an end to the agency’s operations in his city. Mamdani’s joined MS NOW’s Jacob Soboroff for his first media interview since ICE agents shot and wounded Oscar Belgal, 28, during an enforcement operation while he was in his car with his five-year-old child also inside.

The Republican US senator Roger Marshall says he has finally paid off a bakery debt – after six years and repeated collection attempts reported by a Kansas business that had supplied a large order of treats for a 2020 election watch party. “We have absolutely no idea how this happened”, the Kansas senator wrote in a social media post containing a screenshot of the payment on a $678.75 invoice from Holly’s Sweet Treats as well as his $1,300 payment. “And we have repaid the bill … double.”

A businessman wanted for years in the US for allegedly paying bribes to top Venezuelan officials in exchange for lucrative state contracts in Venezuela has been taken into custody. Alvaro Pulido was indicted in Miami federal court in 2019 and again in 2021 as part of an investigation into his longtime business partner, Alex Saab, a one-time ally of ousted Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro.
